groups.note: What each column DOES in a concept's grounding (source-namespaced — every source defines its own; the closed term set is mac.concept.column.role).

terms.meaning: IDENTITY OR JOIN COLUMN. A name resolves TO it through a register; a query then filters or joins on the exact value. Never matched against a label, and never aggregated — an identifier that is summed is a number nobody asked for. Example: `CustomerKey`, what COUNT(DISTINCT) counts and what the fact joins on.

A CATEGORICAL AXIS — legitimate in WHERE and in GROUP BY. Its value domain is either CLOSED (a register states every member, so a non-member is answerable without probing) or OPEN (names resolve through the ladder: exact, normalized, prefix, fuzzy, then ask). Example: `Gender` — `WHERE Gender = 'female'` and `GROUP BY Gender` are both legitimate.

A NUMERIC PAYLOAD. Folded only as its mac.measure_type and the axis allow — the law is stated once there and never restated per concept. Never filtered on directly: a threshold on a measure is a HAVING over the aggregate, not a WHERE over the column. Example: `SalesAmount`.

THE COLUMN A QUESTION'S PERIOD BINDS TO. It says which date is THE reporting date when a relation carries several, so "sales in March" cannot silently pick the wrong one. Example: `OrderDate` on a line that also carries `DeliveryDate`.

PIPELINE BOOKKEEPING, NOT BUSINESS VOCABULARY — validity windows, load stamps, surrogate housekeeping. It is not offered to a question, not grouped on, not filtered on, and its absence from an answer is correct rather than a gap. Example: `StartDT`/`EndDT`, an SCD-2 validity window — when the ROW was written, not when anything happened. Grouping sales by it is meaningless, and until this term existed it was spelled `attribute`, which reads as "a dimension you may not use" rather than "not part of the business at all". NAMED FOR THE MODELLING TRADITION that already has a word for these columns, rather than for the system that writes them: a load stamp is housekeeping whoever keeps the house.

groups.note: The kind of behavioural contract a rule expresses (MAC-core, source-agnostic).

terms.meaning: Identity / matching / scoping of an entity from the question (name, code, key, definition).
Measure math — additivity, period bounds, grain (how a measure may be summed/read).
What to assume when an axis is unspecified but a safe default exists.
An underspecified REQUIRED dimension — ASK, never guess.
What to filter out / never include (pseudo-entries, unmapped rows, stale vintages).
A fact the consumer INHERITS from the serving view (relied on, not re-derived).

groups.note: What kind of thing a concept is (MAC-core). Chosen first; drives which blocks are required.

terms.meaning: A real-world thing with its own identity.
Something that happens — a lifecycle with states / phases.
A numeric fact you aggregate (needs an additivity block).
A closed set of coded values — a lookup / code list (needs a values block).
A dimension / lookup that identifies and describes.
A rollup that groups a leaf concept — e.g. region over country (needs a members block).
A meta-plane concept — about the model itself, not the business data.

groups.note: How trustworthy a concept's definition is — the maturity signal on the Ontology Quality dashboard.

terms.meaning: Confirmed by an SME — authoritative.
Inferred by the harvest (machine) — plausible but not SME-confirmed.
Needs SME input — a known open question / gap.

groups.note: How trustworthy a single rule is (a different scale from concept confidence).

terms.meaning: Confirmed — an SME has signed it off.
Proposed — authored from the schema/context, not yet confirmed (the default).
Rejected — kept for the record but NOT active.

groups.note: How a concept's rows are uniquely identified (MAC-core; mac.concept.identity).

terms.meaning: A universal external standard code (e.g. an ISO country code). Identity = the standard code; local names/labels are aliases.
A closed internal code set (e.g. a fuel or segment code). Identity = the code; surface spellings are aliases.
A code that only means something within a scope — identity = (namespace, code); the bare code collides across scopes. Guarded by mac.canon.composite_key_guard.
An opaque but stable key carrying a resolved human name (e.g. a model code + name). Identity = the key; the name is a joined attribute, not the identity.
Identity is a TUPLE of columns (a fact grain, or a parent+member pair). Keyless-by-design: no single-column key.
Identity not yet known — carried as '__sme__', never invented; graduates to another kind once an SME rules.

groups.note: Per axis, how a measure may be folded (MAC-core; the closed set is mac.concept.aggregation_effect — three terms, replacing the binary additive | non-additive scale at v0.1.15).

terms.meaning: SUM is correct across this axis.

SUM is MEANINGLESS across this axis (a total of durations, rates or ratios is not a number anyone wants); the correct fold is a mean / median / percentile. Not a weaker `additive` — the two disagree about whether the sum means anything.

NO fold is valid along this axis. If a value is needed at a coarser grain it must already EXIST as a stored row: RESOLVE it, never compute it. Which row that is, is determined for the TIME axis by mac_rules.yaml#mac.resolve.period_reading (a bare period reads its END cell) and needs no per-concept rule. Only a NON-time axis whose answer genuinely varies — a reach measure resolving to a matching abstraction level — needs the concept to say.

groups.note: The stage a relationship lives at (MAC-core).

terms.meaning: A stored foreign-key join between the relations.
A semantic relationship between concepts (identity / shared_attribute).
A cross-source relationship (same real-world thing across sources).

groups.note: Every finding the MAC compiler can report — the CLOSED taxonomy, whether or not it fired on this source. A code is the contract: suppressions and counts are keyed on it, so its meaning cannot change without a version bump.

terms.meaning: undefined-artifact — present in the bundle, carries no MAC definition, not declared out of scope
invalid-artifact — has a MAC definition and does not satisfy it
undeclared-extension — an x- key with no profile entry — CONFORMANCE.md §2: undeclared debt, not license
fact-restated — one fact stated in more than one home; nothing keeps the copies in step
fact-contradicted — statements of one fact disagree — something downstream is reading the wrong one
capability-unadopted — MAC offers a mechanism for this and the bundle does not use it
claim-unearned — a conformance level or confidence asserted with no evidence behind it
change-unprotocolled — an authored or tuned object with no entry in the change record
guard-dead — a rule or guard testing a value that cannot occur — it can never fire
reference-unresolved — a reference that resolves to nothing
coverage-missing — a required completeness the bundle does not reach

extension-duplicates-core — an `x-` extension key. Prohibited outright, because it sits BY CONSTRUCTION outside every gate MAC has, so nothing can check what it holds. Measured the day x-grain was retired, TWO of four declared cell keys were false — the main fact view claimed 0 multi-row against millions, and a second fact view claimed 0 against nearly all of its cells. The two that HELD are the two that a view enforces: a view that withholds ambiguous cells, and a current-snapshot view whose collapse makes the key true by construction (its declared cell count reproduced to within a hundred-odd cells). That is the shape of the defect: the declaration is false exactly where nothing makes it true, and a field no gate can reach costs nothing to be wrong in. Three mechanical predicates identify the duplicate case — same subject, same value shape, same closed domain with non-empty overlap. Where there is NO core equivalent the finding is a MAC gap, not a shortcut: say what the wall is and change MAC, rather than declaring beside it. Enforced by tools/check_extension_keys.py, which exits non-zero, because a check that does not block is not enforcement.
